There is no test.

The two most commonly available tests are the RT-PCR (reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction) or an ELISA (enzyme linked immunosorbent assay).

The RT-PCR is done by taking a swab of either the nasal passage or the throat to obtain a sample of the virus. Using a reverse transcriptase and thermal cycling, the genetic material in question is converted from RNA to DNA, then amplified thousands to millions of times by attaching a primer to a specific genetic sequence so that the gene in question can be detected using electrophoresis.

The ELISA is used to detect antibodies, peptides or proteins. There are several different types and I'm not going into them specifically, but the basic idea is that an antibody is specific to what you're trying to detect (and antibodies are extremely specific about their target) is bound to a fixed surface. You introduce your sample (in this case the viral antigen), which then binds to the antigen. A second antibody is introduced that also binds to the viral particle by the variable region of the antibody. The constant region of the secondary antibody is linked to an enzyme that produces either a fluorescent or electrochemical signal when introduced to a reagent.

And of course diseases can exist without showing symptoms. It's called a subclinical infection.

The tests work if they were produced and performed correctly. Just because some products (like the ones from China) are defective doesn't mean they all are.
